predecessors.note: "King Marthanda Varma inherited the small feudal state of Venad in 1723, and built it into Travancore"; "as king of Venad from 1729, employed brutal methods to unify them". venad needs a dossier (listed by sa-03-x).

successors.note: "On 1 July 1949 the kingdom of Travancore was merged with the kingdom of Cochin"; the State of Kerala came into existence on 1 November 1956. travancore-cochin needs a dossier.

capitals.name: Padmanabhapuram
capitals.note: "the capital had been moved in 1601 to Padmanabhapuram, near Kalkulam"; seat until 1795.

capitals.name: Thiruvananthapuram
capitals.note: Dharma Raja "shifted the capital in 1795 from Padmanabhapuram to Thiruvananthapuram".

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. Venad when Marthanda Varma became king in 1729: the page gives no extent; the Kerala coast south of 8.7 N with the Kanyakumari end stands in (about 4,000 km2).
Kollam is the first target in 1731 and Kottarakkara is annexed in 1741 (Marthanda Varma page); the Kerala coast south of 9.05 N.

correction.text: Travancore with Ambalapuzha, Kottayam, Changanassery, Karappuram and Alangad: the kingdom of 1753-1949

keyframe_review.note: Ambalapuzha, Kottayam and Changanassery "by 1753", Karappuram and Alangad ceded by Kochi in 1753. Area about 19,000 km2 against 19,844 km2 on the infobox (1941): ratio 0.96. The page names no later change.

region.text: Venad: Kalkulam and Padmanabhapuram to Thiruvananthapuram

ledger.note: 1729: Marthanda Varma becomes king of Venad and builds Travancore. "as king of Venad from 1729, employed brutal methods to unify them"; infobox "c. 1729 until 1949". He had inherited Venad in 1723.

1731: Marthanda Varma's first target, the port of Kollam (Quilon). "In 1731, the port of Kollam (Quilon)" was the first target, its chief forced to accept annexation after his death; the page also has "between then and 1752, the king annexed Quilon, Kayamkulam, Thekkumkur, Vadakkumkur and Purakkad", so the date of the final annexation is uncertain; Kottarakkara (Elayadathu) follows in 1741.
1741: Elayadathu (Kottarakkara) is annexed. The king was "finally fully annexing the chiefdom to Travancore while the female ruler fled to Kochi"; the Dutch were beaten at Colachel on 10 August 1741.

region.text: Kayamkulam, the northern end of Travancore

ledger.note: 1746: Kayamkulam is annexed. "Travancore now extended from Kanyakumari to Kayamkulam in the north."
1743-1752: Thekkumkur, Vadakkumkur and Purakkad are annexed. "between then and 1752, the king annexed Quilon, Kayamkulam, Thekkumkur, Vadakkumkur and Purakkad."
By 1753: Ambalapuzha, Kottayam and Changanassery are annexed. "Following this, Ambalapuzha, Kottayam and Changanassery were also annexed to Travancore by 1753."

1753: Kochi cedes Karappuram and Alangad. "In 1753, the tributary states of Kochi collectively known as Karappuram and Alangad were ceded to Travancore." The Treaty of Mavelikkara was signed on 15 August 1753.
1795: Dharma Raja moves the capital from Padmanabhapuram to Thiruvananthapuram.

region.text: Travancore with Ambalapuzha, Kottayam, Changanassery, Karappuram and Alangad: the kingdom of 1753-1949

ledger.note: 1 July 1949: Travancore merges with Cochin. "On 1 July 1949 the kingdom of Travancore was merged with the kingdom of Cochin"; it had agreed to accede to the Indian Union on 12 August 1947.

wars.name: Travancore-Dutch War
wars.outcome: Travancore beat the Dutch at Colachel on 10 August 1741; the Treaty of Mavelikkara of 15 August 1753 closed the war. No Dutch territory is on the pages.
wars.note: The Travancore page gives 1739-1753 and elsewhere 1739-46.

wars.name: Annexation of the Kerala principalities

zones.text: Travancore with Ambalapuzha, Kottayam, Changanassery, Karappuram and Alangad: the kingdom of 1753-1949

wars.outcome: Marthanda Varma annexed Kollam, Kottarakkara, Kayamkulam, Thekkumkur, Vadakkumkur, Purakkad, Ambalapuzha, Kottayam and Changanassery between 1731 and 1753; Kochi ceded Karappuram and Alangad; Zamorin of Kozhikode beaten at Purakkad in 1755.

wars.name: Mysore invasion of Travancore
wars.outcome: Tipu Sultan attacked Travancore in 1789 and the Nedunkotta lines on 28 December 1789; the page names no Travancore territory lost.
wars.note: Travancore treated with the British in 1788 and joined a subsidiary alliance in 1795.

certainty.note: Principalities annexed one by one; the pages name chiefdoms and towns, not boundaries, so the shapes are latitude bands of the Kerala coast.
The page gives no boundary line; the northern limit near Alangad is approximate (shape 19,000 km2 against 19,844 km2).

sources.title: Travancore

sources.title: Marthanda Varma
sources.note: Annexations: Kollam 1731, Kottarakkara 1741, Colachel 10 August 1741, Kayamkulam 1746, 1743-52 Thekkumkur/Vadakkumkur/Purakkad, 1753 Ambalapuzha/Kottayam/Changanassery, Mavelikkara 15 August 1753.

notes: Two pages opened (Travancore, Marthanda Varma). Shapes are the Kerala coast cut at latitudes (8.7, 9.05, 9.3, 9.8, 10.2 N) plus a circle for Kanyakumari; the pages date annexations by year spans, so each band is the reading of a span. The Travancore page does not mention Attingal, the Treaty of Mavelikkara details beyond the date, or any Cochin conquest; it dates the British treaties (1788, 1795, 1805) that belong to british-empire (sa-06) as a vassal_start for travancore from 1795 (subsidiary alliance) to 1947. Counterparts needing dossiers: venad (sa-03-x listed it), kingdom-of-cochin, travancore-cochin, Kayamkulam, Elayadathu Swaroopam, Thekkumkur, Vadakkumkur, Ambalapuzha (all minor, Kerala). The 1741 Colachel Dutch defeat moved no Dutch land on the pages opened. Mysore 1789: the page has no territorial result.
